discovery.note: Claude Code is distributed as this npm package, and the nixpkgs `claude-code` derivation packages the same tarball — so the registry's `latest` dist-tag is the version the matrix would move to. `version` is the string `claude --version` printed; the suffix is the harness's own, not an annotation.

The Codex CLI ships to npm and to GitHub releases from the same tag; npm is watched because it is also how a candidate version is materialised on a runner. `version` is the `codex-cli <semver>` string the binary prints.

The Codex desktop app is a long-lived host a consumer configures rather than starts: it has no one-shot invocation, so no matrix cell runs it and there is no version for a run to record. It also self-updates on its own schedule, out of band from any pin this repository could hold, so a discovered version would not describe what any user is running. Its capture path is covered by the lifecycle-hook attribution tests, and keeping up with it stays a manual review.

opencode publishes this npm package per release; the nixpkgs `opencode` derivation tracks the same versions. The binary prints a bare semver, so `version` and `upstream_version` coincide today — they are still recorded separately, because that is a fact about opencode's output format rather than a guarantee.

pi is not in the flake's `matrix` shell, so the ordinary CI matrix skips it and this baseline was seeded from a developer machine rather than from the nixpkgs pin. The npm package is the same artefact, which is what makes pi watchable at all: the drift watch materialises a candidate from this registry, so its cells run in the watch even though they skip in the per-change matrix. Its provenance is therefore the registry's, not a pinned closure's.
